name: Split Markdown into heading chunks for RAG

parameters.content:
### How it works
This workflow helps anyone who has a Markdown file and needs heading-aware chunks for RAG, a notes vault, or a vector database. Click Test workflow to run the sample, or paste your own Markdown into the configuration node. A Code node splits the text by headings first, keeps fenced code blocks and tables together when they fit, and writes one item per chunk. Each chunk includes a heading path, line numbers, a character count, and the text. A last node turns the chunks into a JSONL file you can download from the execution.

This is a simplified built-in splitter. It does not call any paid API. For large files, or for a local CLI and MCP server, use the free tool md-chunk-lite: https://github.com/tidybytetools/md-chunk-lite

### Setup
No accounts or credentials are required. Open the node named "Chunk settings and sample Markdown". Set MAX_CHARS (default 1500) and, if you want, replace SAMPLE_MARKDOWN with your own text. Click Test workflow. Open the output of "Build JSONL file" and download `chunks.jsonl`.

### Customization
Change MAX_CHARS to match your embedding model. Add a node after the chunks if you want to send them to a vector store (that will need credentials, which this template does not include on purpose).
Set MAX_CHARS and paste your Markdown here. The sample is enough for a first run.
One item per chunk, then a JSONL file to download from the execution.

parameters.jsCode:
return [
  {
    json: {
      MAX_CHARS: 1500,
      SAMPLE_MARKDOWN: [
        "# Guide",
        "",
        "Hello.",
        "",
        "## Install",
        "",
        "```bash",
        "pip install tool",
        "```",
        "",
        "## Use",
        "",
        "| a | b |",
        "|---|---|",
        "| 1 | 2 |",
        "",
        "More text after the table.",
        "",
      ].join("\n"),
    },
  },
];
